## Please follow the guide below

- Put an `x` into every box [ ] that applies to your *pull request* (like this: [x])
- Use the *Preview* tab to see how your *pull request* will look

- [ ] [Searched](https://github.com/JarryShaw/PyPCAPKit/pulls?q=is%3Apr) for similar pull requests
- [ ] Followed the [coding style](https://github.com/JarryShaw/PyPCAPKit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style) (`make pylint`, `make mypy`, `make isort`)
- [ ] `make test` passes, and a test case covers the change
- [ ] Described the user-visible change below and left its [changelog entry](https://github.com/JarryShaw/PyPCAPKit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entries) to the maintainer, keeping `docs/source/changelog/` and `CHANGELOG.md` out of the diff, if the change is user-visible

### What is the purpose of your *pull request*?

Tick the [commit type](https://github.com/JarryShaw/PyPCAPKit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#format-of-the-commit-message) your subject line carries.

- [ ] `fix` — corrects a defect
- [ ] `feat` — adds a feature
- [ ] `perf` — changes performance, not behaviour
- [ ] `refactor` — changes neither behaviour nor performance
- [ ] `test` — tests only
- [ ] `docs` — documentation only
- [ ] `ci` — workflows or build tooling
- [ ] `release` — bumps the version or rolls up a distribution
- [ ] `chore` — anything else

- [ ] Also tick if it regenerates constant or registry tables, members keeping their numeric values (the `const` label)

---

### Description of your *pull request* and other information

&emsp; Explanation of your *pull request* goes here: its purpose and effect, and the context and examples a reviewer needs.
